chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

I asked my brother (peace be upon him) about a man who broke an ostrich egg and in the egg were chicks that had moved. He said: 'Upon him is to sacrifice a camel for every chick that moved, slaughtering it in the place of slaughter.'

And when a person in the state of Ihram buys an ostrich egg for a person in Ihram, and the one in Ihram eats it, then upon the buyer is its value: for every egg, one dirham, and upon the buyer, for every egg, a sheep. He narrated.

key_terms.بَعِيرٌ: a camel, used here as a specific expiation sacrifice
key_terms.دِرْهَمٌ: a dirham, a unit of currency
key_terms.مُحِلٌّ: a person who is not in the state of Ihram
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: a person in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking an ostrich egg with a live chick while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific expiation (kaffarah) for breaking an ostrich egg containing a live chick during Ihram, requiring a camel if the chick has moved. It further distinguishes the liability for financial compensation and animal sacrifice when a non-Ihram person purchases the egg for the pilgrim, reflecting the Shia juristic focus on the precise conditions of Ihram violations and their corresponding penalties.
